title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, from commercial microgravity research partnerships to the ongoing evolution of tactical satellite constellations. Meanwhile, the budgetary winds are blowing favorably for space resilience initiatives, even as hypersonic tests continue to stall.

themes.title: Commercial Space Station Partnerships
themes.body: Vast is expanding its network of partners for microgravity research, indicating a growing interest in commercial space applications. This move could pave the way for more robust research opportunities and revenue streams in the sector.

themes.title: Defense Budget Boosts Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added a significant $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, underscoring the government's commitment to fortifying its space assets. This infusion of cash may accelerate development timelines for critical space technologies.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Challenges
themes.body: The third consecutive delay in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing raises questions about the reliability of these technologies. As defense budgets swell, stakeholders will be watching closely to see if this trend continues.

themes.title: Growing Interest in Tactical Satellites
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, reflecting a strategic pivot towards integrated space capabilities. This collaboration signals a competitive landscape as companies vie for contracts in the evolving defense space.
